# Correlation & Regression

## covariance

* can be negative
* dependent on data scale. not used because of this

```
sum((x-x_mean) * (y-y_mean)) / n -1
```

## Correlation Coefficient

```
r = covar(x,y) / sqrt(var(x) * var(y))
```

* between -1 and 1
* level and direction of association between x and y variables
* independent of data scale

With R:
```r
# covariance
cov(x, y, method = "pearson")
# correlation
cor(x, y)
# correlation with p-value
cor.test(x, y)
```

Very sensitive to outliers.

* **Use Spearman test**
    * ranks the data values and correlate the ranks (Wilcox test)
* Common with data with zero-values
    * ex. gene expression data
 
## Linear models
The change in effect is directly proportional to the change in cause

Random errors (residuals) that cause points to deviate from model

* follow normal distribution

Best line

* calculate sum of the square of the errors for each line
* minimize sum = best fit line
    * Will always go through xmean and ymean

Variance of residuals

## R^2

* measure of how much of variance is explained by regression
* Range from 0 - 1:
    * 0 - regression explains none of variance
    * 1 - regression explains all of the variance

```
# Based on residuals
(var(total) - var(residuals)) / var(total)
# Or...
r ** 2
```

residuals

* Must be linear
* Variance must be constant (homoscedasticity)

## Linear models with R
```r
# Exam is dependent variable
# Quiz is the independent variable
ms.lm <- lm(Exam ~ Quiz, data = ms)
ms.lm
```

Then to get rest of stats
```r
summary(ms.lm)
```

To get residuals
```r
ms.lm$residuals
# Or
residuals(ms.lm)
```
